Archive item 1: East Mercia Water Authority Board Minutes – 12 June 2024
Source format: Board meeting minutes

The minutes of the Board meeting held on 8 May 2024, having been circulated, were taken as read.

**Resolved:** That the minutes of the meeting held on 8 May 2024 be approved as a correct record and signed by the Chairman.

*Proposed: Mr J. Barnes*
*Seconded: Mrs E. Whitmore*

---

**3. Matters Arising**

**3.1** Mrs Whitmore reported that the installation of the new telemetry link at Kelham Pumping Station (PS) had been completed on 28 May 2024, ahead of the 31 May target. The link was now feeding live data to the Network Control Centre (NCC). The temporary manual reading regime, which had been in place since April, had been stood down.

**3.2** Mr Singh confirmed that the revised capital programme for the 2024/25 financial year, approved at the May meeting, had been submitted to the regulator on 3 June 2024. The submission included the updated phasing for the Southwell WTW filter refurbishment.

**3.3** Dr Patel raised the question of the customer communication plan for the upcoming planned mains replacement in Bingham. Mr Callaghan confirmed that letters had been issued to all affected properties on 6 June 2024, and that a drop-in session had been arranged for 24 June at Bingham Town Hall.

---

**4. Chairman’s Report**

The Chairman reported on his attendance at the annual conference of the Association of Water Authorities held in Birmingham on 20–21 May 2024. He noted that the conference had focused on resilience planning and the long-term challenges facing the sector. He had held bilateral discussions with the Chief Executive of a neighbouring authority regarding shared contingency arrangements for bulk water supply. A memorandum of understanding was being drafted and would be brought to the Board for consideration at the July meeting.

---

The Board minutes record that East Mercia Water Authority service_area covers Trent Valley District and surrounding areas. Record status: current.

**5. Chief Executive’s Report**

Ms Okafor presented her report for the period 1 May to 11 June 2024. Key points were:

**5.1** Performance against the service area plan for the first quarter of 2024/25 was on track. The service area covering Trent Valley District and surrounding areas had seen a 2.4% reduction in reported leakage incidents compared with the same period last year, although the total volume lost through bursts was slightly up due to two significant main failures in May.

**5.2** Customer satisfaction scores for the quarter stood at 82%, a marginal improvement on the previous quarter. Complaints relating to low pressure in the Edwalton area had been resolved following the completion of the pressure management scheme in April.

**5.3** A draft of the annual resilience statement had been prepared and was undergoing internal review. It would be presented to the Board for approval in September, ahead of the October submission deadline.

**5.4** Staff vacancy levels remained at 4.2%, with particular pressure in the operational technician roles. The recruitment campaign launched in May had attracted a satisfactory number of applications, and interviews were scheduled for late June.

---

**6. Finance Director’s Report**

Mr Singh presented the financial performance report for the period ended 31 May 2024.

**6.1** Revenue for the first two months of the financial year was in line with the budgeted profile. Operating expenditure was 1.1% under budget, primarily due to lower than anticipated electricity costs at the treatment works.

**6.2** The capital programme showed a spend of £4.6 million against a planned £5.2 million for the period. The slippage was attributed to the delayed delivery of pumps for the Radcliffe PS refurbishment, which were now expected on site in early July.
**7. Governance Matters**

**7.1** The Board received the report of the Governance and Audit Committee, which had met on 5 June 2024. The Committee had reviewed the internal audit plan for 2024/25 and noted the progress of the counter-fraud workstream. The Committee also considered the results of the annual review of the Board’s terms of reference and had recommended a small number of drafting amendments, none of which altered the substantive responsibilities of the Board. The amendments were set out in Appendix C.

**7.2** The Board approved the amendments to its terms of reference as recommended by the Committee.

**7.3** Mr Whitmore, the Chair of the Governance and Audit Committee, drew the Board’s attention to the schedule of meetings for the remainder of the calendar year. He reminded members that the Board meets on a monthly basis, with the exception of August when no meeting is scheduled. The schedule for the period July to December 2024 was circulated with the agenda.

**7.4** The Board noted that the schedule of meetings for the 2025/26 municipal year would be brought to the September meeting for approval, in line with the usual practice. The Board minutes indicate East Mercia Water Authority Board meeting_frequency is monthly. Record status: current. The secretariat would continue to publish the schedule on the authority’s website at least fourteen days in advance of each meeting.

**7.5** Mr Whitmore also reported that the Committee had considered the draft annual governance statement, which would be finalised once the external audit opinion had been received. The statement was expected to be brought to the Board for formal approval at the September meeting, alongside the annual resilience statement referred to in the Chief Executive’s report.

**8. Remuneration and Appointments Committee Report**

**8.1** Ms Delaney, Chair of the Remuneration and Appointments Committee, reported on the meeting held on 4 June 2024. The Committee had concluded the annual performance review of the Chief Executive, Ms Okafor, and had agreed the performance-related element of her remuneration for 2024/25. Details of the outcome were recorded in the Committee’s minutes and were not repeated in the public section of the Board minutes, in accordance with the authority’s policy on confidentiality of individual remuneration matters.

**8.2** The Committee had also considered succession planning for senior management roles. A revised succession plan, covering the next three years, had been approved by the Committee and would be kept under annual review. The Board received the report for information.

**9. Forward Plan and Work Programme**

**9.1** The Board considered the forward plan for the next twelve months, which had been circulated as Appendix D. The plan set out the key items expected to come before the Board, including:

**9.1.1** The annual resilience statement for approval in September 2024.

**9.1.2** The outcome of the periodic review of the authority’s charging scheme, expected in November 2024.

**9.1.3** The mid-year review of the service area plan, scheduled for the December 2024 meeting.

**9.1.4** The approval of the 2025/26 budget at the February 2025 meeting.

**9.2** Members were invited to suggest any additional items for the forward plan. Councillor Barnes requested that the Board receive an update on the condition of the strategic water mains in the northern part of the service area, following the two significant main failures in May. The Chief Executive confirmed that a report on the condition assessment programme would be added to the agenda for the September meeting.

**9.3** The Board noted the forward plan and agreed that it should be updated at each meeting, with the secretariat tracking the status of each item.
**10.5** Councillor Barnes asked whether the proposed delegation would apply to the emergency works programme. Mr Achebe confirmed that it would, but noted that the authority’s standing orders already permitted the Director of Operations to incur emergency expenditure up to a separate, lower limit without prior approval, with a requirement to report such expenditure to the next meeting of the Board. The proposed change would not affect that standing order.

**10.6** The Director of Finance confirmed that the proposal had been reviewed by internal audit and that the authority’s financial regulations would need to be amended to reflect the new delegation. He confirmed that the amendment would be drafted and presented to the Board for approval at the September 2024 meeting.

**10.7** The Board discussed the risk implications of the proposed delegation. The Audit and Risk Assurance Committee had considered the proposal at its meeting on 5 June 2024 and had confirmed that the proposed level of delegation was consistent with the authority’s risk appetite. The Committee had noted that the Director of Operations was subject to the authority’s scheme of delegation, which required any exercise of the delegated authority to be recorded in a register of delegated decisions, and that the register was reviewed by the Committee on a quarterly basis.

**10.8** RESOLVED:

That, with effect from 1 July 2024, the Operations Directorate budget_approval_authority is up to £2 million GBP, and that the Director of Operations be authorised to approve expenditure up to that amount within approved budget lines, subject to the conditions set out in the paper and recorded in the authority’s financial regulations.

**10.9** The Board further noted that the decision would be recorded in the Decision Register as EMWA-DR-2024-014, with implementation to be completed by 1 July 2024. The Director of Finance would be responsible for updating the financial regulations and for communicating the change to the relevant staff.

**11. Risk Management Update**

**11.1** The Board received a report from the Director of Finance on the authority’s strategic risk register, which had been reviewed at the meeting of the Audit and Risk Assurance Committee on 5 June 2024. The report highlighted one new risk and one change to an existing risk.

**11.2** A new risk had been added in respect of the condition of the authority’s telemetry and control systems. The risk had been assessed with a current likelihood of three and an impact of four, giving a gross risk score of twelve, which was above the authority’s risk appetite. The mitigating actions included the replacement programme referred to in item 10 above, together with the interim measure of increased remote monitoring of the affected sites. The target risk score, following the completion of the replacement programme, was assessed at six.

**11.3** The existing risk relating to the availability of key operational staff had been reviewed. The likelihood had been increased from three to four, reflecting the difficulties that the authority had experienced in recruiting suitably qualified technicians for the water treatment works. The impact remained at four. The mitigating actions included a review of the recruitment and retention package, which was being undertaken by the Director of People and Organisational Development, and the use of agency staff in the interim.

The Board minutes record Operations Directorate budget_approval_authority as up to £2 million GBP. Record status: current.

**11.4** The Board noted the updated risk register, which had been circulated as Appendix E. The register would be reviewed again at the September 2024 meeting of the Audit and Risk Assurance Committee.

**12. Date of Next Meeting**

**12.1** The next meeting of the Board would be held on 10 July 2024 at the authority’s offices in Mercia House, commencing at 10:00 am.

**13. Close of Meeting**

**13.1** The Chair declared the meeting closed at 3:40 pm.

**Signed:**

*Eleanor Whitmore*

Chair of the Board

Date: 12 June 2024
**14. Supplementary Agenda Items**

**14.1** The Chair reported that, following the circulation of the agenda, two additional items had been identified for consideration at this meeting. These items were taken after the close of the formal agenda and are recorded here as supplementary minutes.

**14.2** The first supplementary item concerned the authority’s response to the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs consultation on the proposed revision to the Security and Emergency Measures Direction. The Director of Operations had prepared a draft response, which had been circulated to Board members under cover of a note dated 6 June 2024.

**14.3** The Director of Operations summarised the key points of the draft response. The authority welcomed the proposed clarification of the roles of Category 1 and Category 2 responders, but had raised a concern about the proposed timescales for the completion of site-specific vulnerability assessments, which the authority considered to be unrealistic given the current capacity constraints within the operational planning team. The draft response also noted that the authority would welcome further guidance on the treatment of telemetry and control systems within the scope of the Direction, particularly in light of the risk referred to in item 11.2 above.

**14.4** The Board discussed the draft response and agreed that the authority’s position should be to support the overall aims of the revision while seeking an extension to the implementation period. The Director of Operations was authorised to submit the response, with the inclusion of the Board’s comments, by the consultation deadline of 28 June 2024.

**14.5** The second supplementary item concerned a request from the Environment Agency for an update on the authority’s progress in implementing the actions arising from the inspection of the Hartford Sewage Treatment Works carried out in March 2024. The request had been received by the authority on 10 June 2024.

**14.6** The Director of Operations reported that good progress had been made on the majority of the actions. The temporary cover for the primary settlement tank had been installed and the flow monitoring equipment at the inlet had been recalibrated. Two actions remained outstanding: the replacement of the failed level sensor on the storm tank, which was awaiting the delivery of a replacement part, and the completion of the revised operating procedure for the desludging operation. Both were expected to be completed by the end of June 2024.

**14.7** The Board noted the update and agreed that the Director of Operations should provide a formal response to the Environment Agency by 18 June 2024, confirming the position and the expected completion dates.

**15. Performance Report for May 2024**

**15.1** The Director of Operations presented the performance report for May 2024, which had been circulated as Appendix F. The report covered the authority’s performance against its key operational and customer service indicators.

**15.2** The Director of Operations drew the Board’s attention to the following points:

- Water quality compliance remained at one hundred per cent for the month. The authority had taken two thousand, one hundred and forty samples during May, all of which had met the required standards.
- The number of properties at risk of low pressure had increased slightly to one hundred and twelve, compared with ninety-eight in April. This was attributed to the warm weather and increased demand, particularly in the north of the area. Work was ongoing to identify the cause of the increase and to implement mitigation measures.
- The number of sewer flooding incidents had remained low, with three incidents reported during the month, all of which had been resolved within the target time.
- The volume of water lost through leakage had been recorded at one hundred and ninety megalitres for the month, which was above the target of one hundred and seventy-five megalitres. The increase was partly due to a burst on a trunk main in the Bishops Lane area of Northgate, which had been repaired within twenty-four hours.
**16. Any Other Business**

**16.1** There being no other business raised under this item, the Chairman invited the Chief Executive to provide a brief verbal update on the outcome of the recent meeting of the Regional Water Resources Group, which had taken place on 5 June 2024.

**16.2** The Chief Executive reported that the Group had considered the draft regional water resources management plan and had noted the progress made by the authority in developing its contribution to the plan. The Group had also discussed the potential for further joint working on demand reduction measures and on the development of a shared approach to the management of the River Lune catchment. No formal decisions had been taken at the meeting, and the next meeting of the Group was scheduled for September 2024.

**16.3** The Chairman thanked the Chief Executive for the update and noted that a written summary of the meeting would be circulated to Board members for information.

**17. Date of Next Meeting**

**17.1** The Board noted that the next ordinary meeting would be held on Wednesday, 10 July 2024, at 10:00 a.m. at the authority’s head office in Northgate. The Chairman reminded members that papers for the meeting would be circulated in accordance with the usual timetable.

**17.2** The Chairman also reminded members that the annual strategy away-day, previously agreed at the meeting held on 8 May 2024, would take place on 4 September 2024. Details of the venue and agenda would be circulated by the Board secretariat in due course.

**18. Thanks and Adjournment**

**18.1** The Chairman expressed the Board’s thanks to the Director of Operations and her team for the comprehensive reports presented at the meeting, and to the Board secretariat for the efficient organisation of the meeting and the timely circulation of papers.

**18.2** There being no further business, the Chairman declared the meeting closed at 12:40 p.m.

**DR-2024-002**
- **Date of Decision:** 15 January 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the procurement of two additional mobile water treatment units (temporary) for use during planned maintenance at Trent Valley Water Treatment Works (WTW).
- **Rationale:** To maintain resilience and ensure continuity of supply to the 250,000 people served by Trent Valley District during the planned shutdown of one treatment stream in Q3 2024. The units will provide a short-term buffer of 15 megalitres per day.
- **Owner:** Head of Water Treatment
- **Budget Reference:** REV-2024-OP-087
- **Risk Assessment:** Low residual risk; units to be mobilised within 72 hours of notice.
- **Status:** Closed. Units mobilised and commissioned 01 September 2024; demobilised 30 September 2024. Final report issued 14 October 2024.

---

**DR-2024-003**
- **Date of Decision:** 26 February 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the introduction of a seasonal demand management tariff for large non-household customers in Trent Valley District, effective from 01 June 2024.
- **Rationale:** To reduce peak demand pressure on the distribution network during summer months and defer the need for a new service reservoir.
- **Owner:** Director of Customer Services
- **Budget Reference:** REV-2024-CM-112
- **Risk Assessment:** Medium; potential customer dissatisfaction mitigated by a 12-month notice period for affected customers.
- **Status:** In progress. Tariff published 01 May 2024; first billing cycle under new tariff scheduled for July 2024.

---

The decision register cites Trent Valley District population_served as 250000 people. Record status: current.

**DR-2024-004**
- **Date of Decision:** 18 March 2024
- **Decision:** Approve a 12-month trial of a new leak detection technology (satellite-based) covering the rural parts of Trent Valley District.
- **Rationale:** Current acoustic surveys cover only 40% of the network per year; satellite technology offers a potential to identify leaks in areas with low population density and long mains runs, reducing non-revenue water (NRW).
- **Owner:** Head of Network Operations
- **Budget Reference:** CAP-2024-OP-031
- **Risk Assessment:** Low; trial costs are capped at £180,000; no impact on supply.
- **Status:** In progress. Trial commenced 01 May 2024; initial survey data received 30 June 2024; analysis ongoing.

---

**DR-2024-005**
- **Date of Decision:** 22 April 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the recruitment of two additional water quality sampling officers (permanent) to support increased regulatory sampling frequency in Trent Valley District.
- **Rationale:** New regulatory requirements under the Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016 (as amended) require additional sampling at customer taps; current staffing levels are insufficient to meet the schedule without overtime.
- **Owner:** Director of Quality & Environment
- **Budget Reference:** REV-2024-HR-024
- **Risk Assessment:** Low; recruitment market is competitive, but roles have been advertised at a market-adjusted salary.

**DR-2024-006**

- **Rationale:** The deferral is to align with the proposed regional grid investment programme, which may alter the abstraction strategy. The main will be subject to enhanced condition monitoring in the interim.
- **Owner:** Director of Capital Delivery
- **Budget Reference:** CAP-2024-OP-052 (deferred)
- **Risk Assessment:** Medium; the main is in service and has a current condition grade of 2 (good). Enhanced monitoring will be implemented from 01 July 2024. A re-evaluation is scheduled for Q1 2025.
- **Status:** Suspended. Decision to be reviewed by the Board in January 2025.

**DR-2024-007**
- **Date of Decision:** 17 June 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the award of a three-year framework contract for the supply and delivery of sodium hypochlorite (12.5% solution) for disinfection at all water treatment works in the Authority’s operational area.
- **Rationale:** The existing supply agreement expires on 30 September 2024. The framework will secure continuity of supply at a fixed unit price, with provision for quarterly price adjustment linked to published chemical indices. The tender exercise received six compliant bids; the recommended supplier offered the lowest whole-life cost and demonstrated adequate resilience in its supply chain.
- **Owner:** Director of Procurement & Commercial Services
- **Budget Reference:** REV-2024-OPS-047
- **Risk Assessment:** Low. Stock levels at all WTWs are sufficient for a minimum of 14 days at normal consumption rates. A contingency arrangement with the second-ranked bidder has been noted in the contract file but not activated.
- **Status:** Closed. Contract executed 01 August 2024; first delivery under the new framework received 02 October 2024.

---

**DR-2024-008**
- **Date of Decision:** 15 July 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the implementation of a temporary reduction in the chlorine residual set-point at four service reservoirs in the South Wolds supply zone, from 0.50 mg/l to 0.40 mg/l, for a trial period of six months.
- **Rationale:** Customer complaints regarding taste and odour in the zone have been persistent since spring. The water quality team assessed that a modest reduction in the residual, while maintaining compliance with the minimum residual requirement, may alleviate the issue without compromising microbiological safety. The trial will be supported by enhanced bacteriological sampling at the reservoir outlets and at 20 customer taps per month.
- **Owner:** Director of Quality & Environment
- **Budget Reference:** REV-2024-WQ-061
- **Risk Assessment:** Medium. Any exceedance of the microbiological parameters at the trial sites will trigger an immediate return to the previous set-point. The trial is subject to a formal review after four months; the Board will be notified of the outcome.
- **Status:** In progress. Trial commenced 01 August 2024. Interim sampling data (August and September) show no adverse bacteriological results; taste and odour complaints in the zone have reduced by approximately 30% compared with the same period last year. Review scheduled for December 2024.

**DR-2024-009**
- **Date of Decision:** 12 August 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the procurement of a new telemetry master station software upgrade, including a migration to a hosted (cloud-based) infrastructure, with a target go-live date of 31 March 2025.
- **Rationale:** The current on-premises telemetry system is reaching end-of-life; the supplier has announced cessation of support for the existing software version after 31 December 2025. The upgrade is required to maintain reliable remote monitoring and control of pumping stations, service reservoirs, and the distribution network. The hosted solution was selected following a technical options appraisal which identified lower whole-life cost and improved resilience.
- **Owner:** Head of Network Operations
- **Budget Reference:** CAP-2024-IT-018
- **Risk Assessment:** High. The telemetry system is critical to operational control. Migration will be phased by geographic region, with each phase subject to a parallel-run period of not less than two weeks. A rollback plan is in place. The Network Control Centre (NCC) will maintain enhanced manual monitoring procedures during the migration windows.
- **Status:** In progress. Contract awarded 01 September 2024; detailed design completed 30 October 2024. Migration of the first region (North Wolds) is scheduled to commence 06 January 2025.

documents.content:
The minutes of the Board meeting held on 8 May 2024, having been circulated, were taken as read.

**Resolved:** That the minutes of the meeting held on 8 May 2024 be approved as a correct record and signed by the Chairman.

*Proposed: Mr J. Barnes*
*Seconded: Mrs E. Whitmore*

---

**3. Matters Arising**

**3.1** Mrs Whitmore reported that the installation of the new telemetry link at Kelham Pumping Station (PS) had been completed on 28 May 2024, ahead of the 31 May target. The link was now feeding live data to the Network Control Centre (NCC). The temporary manual reading regime, which had been in place since April, had been stood down.

**3.2** Mr Singh confirmed that the revised capital programme for the 2024/25 financial year, approved at the May meeting, had been submitted to the regulator on 3 June 2024. The submission included the updated phasing for the Southwell WTW filter refurbishment.

**3.3** Dr Patel raised the question of the customer communication plan for the upcoming planned mains replacement in Bingham. Mr Callaghan confirmed that letters had been issued to all affected properties on 6 June 2024, and that a drop-in session had been arranged for 24 June at Bingham Town Hall.

---

**4. Chairman’s Report**

The Chairman reported on his attendance at the annual conference of the Association of Water Authorities held in Birmingham on 20–21 May 2024. He noted that the conference had focused on resilience planning and the long-term challenges facing the sector. He had held bilateral discussions with the Chief Executive of a neighbouring authority regarding shared contingency arrangements for bulk water supply. A memorandum of understanding was being drafted and would be brought to the Board for consideration at the July meeting.

---

The Board minutes record that East Mercia Water Authority service_area covers Trent Valley District and surrounding areas. Record status: current.

**5. Chief Executive’s Report**

Ms Okafor presented her report for the period 1 May to 11 June 2024. Key points were:

**5.1** Performance against the service area plan for the first quarter of 2024/25 was on track. The service area covering Trent Valley District and surrounding areas had seen a 2.4% reduction in reported leakage incidents compared with the same period last year, although the total volume lost through bursts was slightly up due to two significant main failures in May.

**5.2** Customer satisfaction scores for the quarter stood at 82%, a marginal improvement on the previous quarter. Complaints relating to low pressure in the Edwalton area had been resolved following the completion of the pressure management scheme in April.

**5.3** A draft of the annual resilience statement had been prepared and was undergoing internal review. It would be presented to the Board for approval in September, ahead of the October submission deadline.

**5.4** Staff vacancy levels remained at 4.2%, with particular pressure in the operational technician roles. The recruitment campaign launched in May had attracted a satisfactory number of applications, and interviews were scheduled for late June.

---

**6. Finance Director’s Report**

Mr Singh presented the financial performance report for the period ended 31 May 2024.

**6.1** Revenue for the first two months of the financial year was in line with the budgeted profile. Operating expenditure was 1.1% under budget, primarily due to lower than anticipated electricity costs at the treatment works.

**6.2** The capital programme showed a spend of £4.6 million against a planned £5.2 million for the period. The slippage was attributed to the delayed delivery of pumps for the Radcliffe PS refurbishment, which were now expected on site in early July.

The statement was expected to be brought to the Board for formal approval at the September meeting, alongside the annual resilience statement referred to in the Chief Executive’s report.

**8. Remuneration and Appointments Committee Report**

**8.1** Ms Delaney, Chair of the Remuneration and Appointments Committee, reported on the meeting held on 4 June 2024. The Committee had concluded the annual performance review of the Chief Executive, Ms Okafor, and had agreed the performance-related element of her remuneration for 2024/25. Details of the outcome were recorded in the Committee’s minutes and were not repeated in the public section of the Board minutes, in accordance with the authority’s policy on confidentiality of individual remuneration matters.

**8.2** The Committee had also considered succession planning for senior management roles. A revised succession plan, covering the next three years, had been approved by the Committee and would be kept under annual review. The Board received the report for information.

**9.1.4** The approval of the 2025/26 budget at the February 2025 meeting.

Councillor Barnes requested that the Board receive an update on the condition of the strategic water mains in the northern part of the service area, following the two significant main failures in May. The Chief Executive confirmed that a report on the condition assessment programme would be added to the agenda for the September meeting.

The Audit and Risk Assurance Committee had considered the proposal at its meeting on 5 June 2024 and had confirmed that the proposed level of delegation was consistent with the authority’s risk appetite. The Committee had noted that the Director of Operations was subject to the authority’s scheme of delegation, which required any exercise of the delegated authority to be recorded in a register of delegated decisions, and that the register was reviewed by the Committee on a quarterly basis.

**10.8** RESOLVED:

That, with effect from 1 July 2024, the Operations Directorate budget_approval_authority is up to £2 million GBP, and that the Director of Operations be authorised to approve expenditure up to that amount within approved budget lines, subject to the conditions set out in the paper and recorded in the authority’s financial regulations.

**10.9** The Board further noted that the decision would be recorded in the Decision Register as EMWA-DR-2024-014, with implementation to be completed by 1 July 2024. The Director of Finance would be responsible for updating the financial regulations and for communicating the change to the relevant staff.

**11. Risk Management Update**

**11.1** The Board received a report from the Director of Finance on the authority’s strategic risk register, which had been reviewed at the meeting of the Audit and Risk Assurance Committee on 5 June 2024. The report highlighted one new risk and one change to an existing risk.

**11.2** A new risk had been added in respect of the condition of the authority’s telemetry and control systems. The risk had been assessed with a current likelihood of three and an impact of four, giving a gross risk score of twelve, which was above the authority’s risk appetite. The mitigating actions included the replacement programme referred to in item 10 above, together with the interim measure of increased remote monitoring of the affected sites. The target risk score, following the completion of the replacement programme, was assessed at six.

**11.3** The existing risk relating to the availability of key operational staff had been reviewed. The likelihood had been increased from three to four, reflecting the difficulties that the authority had experienced in recruiting suitably qualified technicians for the water treatment works. The impact remained at four. The mitigating actions included a review of the recruitment and retention package, which was being undertaken by the Director of People and Organisational Development, and the use of agency staff in the interim.

The Board minutes record Operations Directorate budget_approval_authority as up to £2 million GBP. Record status: current.

**11.4** The Board noted the updated risk register, which had been circulated as Appendix E. The register would be reviewed again at the September 2024 meeting of the Audit and Risk Assurance Committee.

**12. Date of Next Meeting**

documents.content:
**14. Supplementary Agenda Items**

**14.1** The Chair reported that, following the circulation of the agenda, two additional items had been identified for consideration at this meeting. These items were taken after the close of the formal agenda and are recorded here as supplementary minutes.

**14.2** The first supplementary item concerned the authority’s response to the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs consultation on the proposed revision to the Security and Emergency Measures Direction. The Director of Operations had prepared a draft response, which had been circulated to Board members under cover of a note dated 6 June 2024.

**14.3** The Director of Operations summarised the key points of the draft response. The authority welcomed the proposed clarification of the roles of Category 1 and Category 2 responders, but had raised a concern about the proposed timescales for the completion of site-specific vulnerability assessments, which the authority considered to be unrealistic given the current capacity constraints within the operational planning team. The draft response also noted that the authority would welcome further guidance on the treatment of telemetry and control systems within the scope of the Direction, particularly in light of the risk referred to in item 11.2 above.

**14.4** The Board discussed the draft response and agreed that the authority’s position should be to support the overall aims of the revision while seeking an extension to the implementation period. The Director of Operations was authorised to submit the response, with the inclusion of the Board’s comments, by the consultation deadline of 28 June 2024.

**14.5** The second supplementary item concerned a request from the Environment Agency for an update on the authority’s progress in implementing the actions arising from the inspection of the Hartford Sewage Treatment Works carried out in March 2024. The request had been received by the authority on 10 June 2024.

**14.6** The Director of Operations reported that good progress had been made on the majority of the actions. The temporary cover for the primary settlement tank had been installed and the flow monitoring equipment at the inlet had been recalibrated. Two actions remained outstanding: the replacement of the failed level sensor on the storm tank, which was awaiting the delivery of a replacement part, and the completion of the revised operating procedure for the desludging operation. Both were expected to be completed by the end of June 2024.

**14.7** The Board noted the update and agreed that the Director of Operations should provide a formal response to the Environment Agency by 18 June 2024, confirming the position and the expected completion dates.

**15. Performance Report for May 2024**

**15.1** The Director of Operations presented the performance report for May 2024, which had been circulated as Appendix F. The report covered the authority’s performance against its key operational and customer service indicators.

**15.2** The Director of Operations drew the Board’s attention to the following points:

- Water quality compliance remained at one hundred per cent for the month. The authority had taken two thousand, one hundred and forty samples during May, all of which had met the required standards.
- The number of properties at risk of low pressure had increased slightly to one hundred and twelve, compared with ninety-eight in April. This was attributed to the warm weather and increased demand, particularly in the north of the area. Work was ongoing to identify the cause of the increase and to implement mitigation measures.
- The number of sewer flooding incidents had remained low, with three incidents reported during the month, all of which had been resolved within the target time.
- The volume of water lost through leakage had been recorded at one hundred and ninety megalitres for the month, which was above the target of one hundred and seventy-five megalitres. The increase was partly due to a burst on a trunk main in the Bishops Lane area of Northgate, which had been repaired within twenty-four hours.

documents.content:
---

**DR-2024-002**
- **Date of Decision:** 15 January 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the procurement of two additional mobile water treatment units (temporary) for use during planned maintenance at Trent Valley Water Treatment Works (WTW).
- **Rationale:** To maintain resilience and ensure continuity of supply to the 250,000 people served by Trent Valley District during the planned shutdown of one treatment stream in Q3 2024. The units will provide a short-term buffer of 15 megalitres per day.
- **Owner:** Head of Water Treatment
- **Budget Reference:** REV-2024-OP-087
- **Risk Assessment:** Low residual risk; units to be mobilised within 72 hours of notice.
- **Status:** Closed. Units mobilised and commissioned 01 September 2024; demobilised 30 September 2024. Final report issued 14 October 2024.

---

**DR-2024-003**
- **Date of Decision:** 26 February 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the introduction of a seasonal demand management tariff for large non-household customers in Trent Valley District, effective from 01 June 2024.
- **Rationale:** To reduce peak demand pressure on the distribution network during summer months and defer the need for a new service reservoir.
- **Owner:** Director of Customer Services
- **Budget Reference:** REV-2024-CM-112
- **Risk Assessment:** Medium; potential customer dissatisfaction mitigated by a 12-month notice period for affected customers.
- **Status:** In progress. Tariff published 01 May 2024; first billing cycle under new tariff scheduled for July 2024.

---

The decision register cites Trent Valley District population_served as 250000 people. Record status: current.

**DR-2024-004**
- **Date of Decision:** 18 March 2024
- **Decision:** Approve a 12-month trial of a new leak detection technology (satellite-based) covering the rural parts of Trent Valley District.
- **Rationale:** Current acoustic surveys cover only 40% of the network per year; satellite technology offers a potential to identify leaks in areas with low population density and long mains runs, reducing non-revenue water (NRW).
- **Owner:** Head of Network Operations
- **Budget Reference:** CAP-2024-OP-031
- **Risk Assessment:** Low; trial costs are capped at £180,000; no impact on supply.
- **Status:** In progress. Trial commenced 01 May 2024; initial survey data received 30 June 2024; analysis ongoing.

---

**DR-2024-005**
- **Date of Decision:** 22 April 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the recruitment of two additional water quality sampling officers (permanent) to support increased regulatory sampling frequency in Trent Valley District.
- **Rationale:** New regulatory requirements under the Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016 (as amended) require additional sampling at customer taps; current staffing levels are insufficient to meet the schedule without overtime.
- **Owner:** Director of Quality & Environment
- **Budget Reference:** REV-2024-HR-024
- **Risk Assessment:** Low; recruitment market is competitive, but roles have been advertised at a market-adjusted salary.
- **Status:** Closed. Both posts filled; officers commenced duties 01 July 2024.

---

**DR-2024-006**
- **Date of Decision:** 20 May 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the deferral of the planned replacement of a portion of the raw water main between Trent Valley WTW and the river abstraction point, originally scheduled for 2024/25.
- **Rationale:** The deferral is to align with the proposed regional grid investment programme, which may alter the abstraction strategy. The main will be subject to enhanced condition monitoring in the interim.
- **Owner:** Director of Capital Delivery
- **Budget Reference:** CAP-2024-OP-052 (deferred)
- **Risk Assessment:** Medium; the main is in service and has a current condition grade of 2 (good). Enhanced monitoring will be implemented from 01 July 2024. A re-evaluation is scheduled for Q1 2025.
- **Status:** Suspended. Decision to be reviewed by the Board in January 2025.

**East Mercia Water Authority Decision Register 2024**

---

**DR-2024-007**
- **Date of Decision:** 17 June 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the award of a three-year framework contract for the supply and delivery of sodium hypochlorite (12.5% solution) for disinfection at all water treatment works in the Authority’s operational area.
- **Rationale:** The existing supply agreement expires on 30 September 2024. The framework will secure continuity of supply at a fixed unit price, with provision for quarterly price adjustment linked to published chemical indices. The tender exercise received six compliant bids; the recommended supplier offered the lowest whole-life cost and demonstrated adequate resilience in its supply chain.
- **Owner:** Director of Procurement & Commercial Services
- **Budget Reference:** REV-2024-OPS-047
- **Risk Assessment:** Low. Stock levels at all WTWs are sufficient for a minimum of 14 days at normal consumption rates. A contingency arrangement with the second-ranked bidder has been noted in the contract file but not activated.
- **Status:** Closed. Contract executed 01 August 2024; first delivery under the new framework received 02 October 2024.

---

**DR-2024-008**
- **Date of Decision:** 15 July 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the implementation of a temporary reduction in the chlorine residual set-point at four service reservoirs in the South Wolds supply zone, from 0.50 mg/l to 0.40 mg/l, for a trial period of six months.
- **Rationale:** Customer complaints regarding taste and odour in the zone have been persistent since spring. The water quality team assessed that a modest reduction in the residual, while maintaining compliance with the minimum residual requirement, may alleviate the issue without compromising microbiological safety. The trial will be supported by enhanced bacteriological sampling at the reservoir outlets and at 20 customer taps per month.
- **Owner:** Director of Quality & Environment
- **Budget Reference:** REV-2024-WQ-061
- **Risk Assessment:** Medium. Any exceedance of the microbiological parameters at the trial sites will trigger an immediate return to the previous set-point. The trial is subject to a formal review after four months; the Board will be notified of the outcome.
- **Status:** In progress. Trial commenced 01 August 2024. Interim sampling data (August and September) show no adverse bacteriological results; taste and odour complaints in the zone have reduced by approximately 30% compared with the same period last year. Review scheduled for December 2024.

---

**DR-2024-009**
- **Date of Decision:** 12 August 2024
- **Decision:** Approve the procurement of a new telemetry master station software upgrade, including a migration to a hosted (cloud-based) infrastructure, with a target go-live date of 31 March 2025.
- **Rationale:** The current on-premises telemetry system is reaching end-of-life; the supplier has announced cessation of support for the existing software version after 31 December 2025. The upgrade is required to maintain reliable remote monitoring and control of pumping stations, service reservoirs, and the distribution network. The hosted solution was selected following a technical options appraisal which identified lower whole-life cost and improved resilience.
- **Owner:** Head of Network Operations
- **Budget Reference:** CAP-2024-IT-018
- **Risk Assessment:** High. The telemetry system is critical to operational control. Migration will be phased by geographic region, with each phase subject to a parallel-run period of not less than two weeks. A rollback plan is in place. The Network Control Centre (NCC) will maintain enhanced manual monitoring procedures during the migration windows.
- **Status:** In progress. Contract awarded 01 September 2024; detailed design completed 30 October 2024. Migration of the first region (North Wolds) is scheduled to commence 06 January 2025.
